questions.question: A force of 500 N acts perpendicular to an area of 0.25 m². What is the pressure produced in Pascals?
What is the liquid pressure in Pascals at a depth of 5 meters in pure water? (Density = 1000 kg/m³, g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.explanation: P = hρg = 5 m × 1000 kg/m³ × 9.8 m/s² = 49000 Pa.

questions.question: An object of density 800 kg/m³ floats in water of density 1000 kg/m³. What percentage of the object's volume is submerged under water?
questions.explanation: Submerged fraction = ρ_body / ρ_liquid = 800 / 1000 = 0.80 = 80%.

questions.question: How much heat energy in Joules is required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of water by 10°C? (Specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J/(kg·K))
A radioactive sample has a half-life of 10 days. After 30 days, what fraction of the original radioactive nuclei remains?
questions.explanation: Number of half-lives n = 30 / 10 = 3. Remaining fraction = (1/2)³ = 1/8.

questions.question: Which medical imaging modality provides the highest soft-tissue contrast without using any ionizing radiation?
questions.correct_answer: mri
questions.explanation: MRI uses non-ionizing magnetic fields and radiofrequency pulses to map hydrogen density, providing unmatched soft-tissue visualization.

questions.question: What radioactive particle consists of two protons and two neutrons bound together into a helium nucleus?
questions.correct_answer: alpha particle
questions.explanation: An alpha particle is a Helium-4 nucleus (⁴₂He²⁺) emitted during alpha decay of heavy radionuclides.

questions.question: At what specific temperature on the Celsius scale does liquid water achieve its maximum density?
questions.explanation: Due to anomalous expansion, liquid water reaches its maximum density of 1000 kg/m³ at 4°C.

questions.question: Which medical diagnostic technique detects real-time blood flow direction and velocity using ultrasound frequency shifts?
questions.correct_answer: doppler ultrasound
questions.explanation: Doppler ultrasound measures the frequency shift of sound waves reflected from moving erythrocytes to evaluate vascular blood flow.

questions.question: What type of wave represents ventricular depolarization on a clinical electrocardiogram (ECG) tracing?
questions.correct_answer: qrs complex
questions.explanation: The QRS complex represents the electrical depolarization wave sweeping through the ventricles immediately before ventricular contraction.

questions.question: A hydraulic press has a master cylinder with a piston radius of 2 cm and a slave cylinder with a piston radius of 20 cm. If a force of 100 N is applied to the master piston, what force does the slave piston exert?
A solid cylinder of mass 4 kg and volume 0.005 m³ is suspended completely submerged in oil of density 800 kg/m³. What is the tension in the supporting string? (g = 10 m/s²)
options: 0 N (floats freely)
questions.correct_answer: 0 N (floats freely)
questions.explanation: Downward weight W = mg = 4 × 10 = 40 N. Upward buoyant force F_B = V × ρ_oil × g = 0.005 × 800 × 10 = 40 N. Net downward force T = W - F_B = 40 - 40 = 0 N.

questions.question: A steel rod of initial length 5.0 m is heated from 15°C to 65°C. If the linear expansion coefficient of steel is 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹, what is the rod's final length?
An aluminum kettle of mass 0.5 kg contains 1.0 kg of water, both at 20°C. How much heat is needed to bring the water to 100°C? (s_water = 4200 J/(kg·K), s_Al = 900 J/(kg·K))
How many kilograms of ice at 0°C can be completely melted by 1,008,000 Joules of heat? (Latent heat of fusion = 3.36 × 10⁵ J/kg)
options: 3 kg
1.5 kg
6 kg
questions.correct_answer: 3 kg

questions.question: A sample of Radon-222 has a half-life of 3.8 days. If its initial activity is 1600 Bq, how many days will it take for the activity to fall to 100 Bq?
options: 15.2 days
11.4 days
7.6 days
19.0 days
questions.correct_answer: 15.2 days
questions.explanation: Activity drops from 1600 → 800 → 400 → 200 → 100 Bq (4 half-lives). Total time = 4 × 3.8 days = 15.2 days.

questions.question: An elephant of mass 4000 kg stands evenly on all four feet. Each foot has a circular ground contact area of 0.05 m². What pressure does the elephant exert on the ground? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Total force F = mg = 4000 × 10 = 40,000 N. Total area for 4 feet A = 4 × 0.05 = 0.20 m². Pressure P = 40,000 / 0.20 = 200,000 Pa (200 kPa).

questions.question: A rectangular swimming pool has dimensions 20 m long, 10 m wide, and 2 m deep, completely filled with water (density = 1000 kg/m³). What is the total thrust force exerted by water on the bottom floor? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Floor area A = 20 × 10 = 200 m². Bottom pressure P = hρg = 2 × 1000 × 10 = 20,000 Pa. Total thrust F = P × A = 20,000 Pa × 200 m² = 4.0 × 10⁶ N.

questions.question: A copper wire of length 3 m and diameter 2 mm is stretched by a load of 100 N. If Young's modulus for copper is 1.1 × 10¹¹ Pa, what is the extension produced?
A piece of glass weighs 2.5 N in air and 1.5 N when submerged in water. What is the volume of the glass? (Density of water = 1000 kg/m³, g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Buoyant force F_B = 2.5 - 1.5 = 1.0 N. Volume V = F_B / (ρ_water × g) = 1.0 / (1000 × 10) = 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ m³ (100 cm³).

questions.question: An X-ray tube operates with a tube current of 10 mA (0.01 A). How many electrons strike the tungsten target per second? (Charge of electron = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C)
questions.explanation: n = I / e = (0.01 C/s) / (1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) = 6.25 × 10¹⁶ electrons per second.

questions.question: In a nuclear reaction, a mass defect of 1.0 × 10⁻⁶ kg (1 mg) is completely converted into energy. How much energy in Joules is released? (c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)

A lead bullet of mass 0.02 kg moving at 200 m/s hits a wooden block and comes to rest. Assuming all kinetic energy is converted into heat inside the bullet, what is its temperature rise? (Specific heat capacity of lead = 130 J/(kg·K))
A 100 cm³ glass container is full of mercury at 0°C. How much mercury will overflow if temperature rises to 50°C? (γ_mercury = 18 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹, γ_glass = 2.4 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹)
options: 0.78 cm³
0.90 cm³
0.12 cm³
1.02 cm³
questions.correct_answer: 0.78 cm³
questions.explanation: Apparent expansion γ_apparent = γ_mercury - γ_glass = (18 - 2.4) × 10⁻⁵ = 15.6 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹. Overflow ΔV = V × γ_app × ΔT = 100 × (15.6 × 10⁻⁵) × 50 = 0.78 cm³.

questions.question: A clinical ultrasound scanner detects a Doppler frequency shift of 2 kHz from a blood vessel when using a 5 MHz probe (speed of sound in tissue = 1540 m/s). If beam angle θ = 0° (cos θ = 1), what is blood velocity?
How much work is done against gravity to pump 1000 liters (1 m³) of water to the rooftop tank of a 15-meter building? (Density of water = 1000 kg/m³, g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Mass m = 1000 kg. Work W = mgh = 1000 kg × 9.8 m/s² × 15 m = 147,000 Joules.

questions.question: Why does a piece of cork float with most of its volume above water, while a piece of oak floats with most of its volume submerged?
options: Cork has a much lower density (~240 kg/m³) than oak (~750 kg/m³), requiring less displaced water to match its weight
Cork contains magnetic pockets that repel water molecules
Oak wood is chemically soluble in water
Water exerts greater buoyant force on lighter materials
questions.correct_answer: Cork has a much lower density (~240 kg/m³) than oak (~750 kg/m³), requiring less displaced water to match its weight
questions.explanation: By the law of floatation, V_submerged / V_total = ρ_wood / ρ_water. Cork's low density means only ~24% is submerged, whereas denser oak must submerge ~75% to generate sufficient upthrust.

questions.question: Why do deep-sea fish explode or suffer severe barotrauma when hauled rapidly to the ocean surface?
options: Their internal body fluids are equilibrated to immense deep-sea hydrostatic pressures; sudden surface decompression causes internal gases to expand violently
Sunlight is poisonous to deep-sea marine biology
Seawater at the surface contains too much oxygen
Surface waves heat the fish to boiling temperatures
questions.correct_answer: Their internal body fluids are equilibrated to immense deep-sea hydrostatic pressures; sudden surface decompression causes internal gases to expand violently
questions.explanation: At depths of thousands of meters, ambient hydrostatic pressure P = hρg is hundreds of atmospheres. Rapid ascent drops external pressure, causing dissolved gases in tissues and swim bladders to expand catastrophically (Boyle's Law).

questions.question: What is the physical mechanism by which a drinking straw draws beverage liquid up into the mouth?
options: Expanding lungs and mouth cavity lowers internal air pressure, allowing higher atmospheric pressure outside to push the liquid up
The plastic straw exerts electrostatic suction on the liquid
Capillary action alone pulls the drink upward against gravity
Liquid molecules are repelled by air in the straw
questions.correct_answer: Expanding lungs and mouth cavity lowers internal air pressure, allowing higher atmospheric pressure outside to push the liquid up
questions.explanation: Sucking removes air from inside the straw, creating a partial vacuum. The higher atmospheric pressure acting on the open surface of the drink pushes the fluid up the straw.

questions.question: Why does a clinical glass fever thermometer feature a narrow constriction in the capillary bore just above the mercury bulb?
options: To prevent the expanded mercury thread from falling back into the bulb when removed from the patient's mouth
To slow down the initial expansion of mercury during reading
To filter out air bubbles from entering the mercury reservoir
To allow the doctor to reset the temperature without shaking
questions.correct_answer: To prevent the expanded mercury thread from falling back into the bulb when removed from the patient's mouth
questions.explanation: The constriction allows expanding mercury to push past during measurement, but breaks the mercury column when cooling begins, freezing the peak temperature reading until vigorously shaken down.

questions.question: Why does a large body of water (like an ocean or large lake) moderate the climate of nearby coastal lands, preventing extreme heat or cold?
options: Water has an exceptionally high specific heat capacity, absorbing immense solar heat in summer and releasing it slowly in winter with small temperature changes
Ocean water reflects 100% of atmospheric coldness back into space
Water molecules generate geothermal heat continuously
Evaporation creates a permanent greenhouse cloud layer over coastal towns
questions.correct_answer: Water has an exceptionally high specific heat capacity, absorbing immense solar heat in summer and releasing it slowly in winter with small temperature changes
questions.explanation: Water's high specific heat (4200 J/(kg·K)) is roughly five times that of soil and rock. It acts as a massive thermal buffer, absorbing summer heat without rising much in temperature and releasing it during winter.

questions.question: Why does sweating cool the human body efficiently during vigorous exercise?
options: Evaporation of each gram of perspiration extracts 2.26 × 10⁶ J/kg of latent heat of vaporization directly from the skin
Sweat dissolves hot thermal particles on the skin surface
Sweat creates cold ice crystals across skin pores
Perspiration blocks incoming sunlight from reaching blood vessels
questions.correct_answer: Evaporation of each gram of perspiration extracts 2.26 × 10⁶ J/kg of latent heat of vaporization directly from the skin
questions.explanation: Perspiration utilizes the large latent heat of vaporization of water (2.26 × 10⁶ J/kg). Evaporating moisture draws thermal energy directly from cutaneous blood vessels, stabilizing core body temperature.

questions.question: Why does an electric current flow in a forward-biased p-n junction diode, whereas virtually no current flows under reverse bias?
options: Forward bias opposes and reduces the built-in potential barrier, enabling majority carriers to cross; reverse bias widens the barrier
Reverse bias destroys the semiconductor crystal permanently
Forward bias generates new radioactive alpha particles at the junction
Reverse bias converts silicon atoms into copper
questions.correct_answer: Forward bias opposes and reduces the built-in potential barrier, enabling majority carriers to cross; reverse bias widens the barrier
questions.explanation: Forward bias pushes majority electrons in n-region and holes in p-region toward the junction, thinning the depletion region. Reverse bias pulls carriers away from the junction, widening the insulating depletion layer.

questions.question: Why is Lead-206 (²⁰⁶₈₂Pb) the final stable end-product of the Uranium-238 radioactive decay series?
options: Its magic numbers of nucleons give it a tightly bound, highly stable nuclear configuration that undergoes no further spontaneous decay
It has the largest mass of any element on Earth
Lead absorbs all incoming cosmic rays to stay stable
Uranium atoms stop decaying when they run out of electrons
questions.correct_answer: Its magic numbers of nucleons give it a tightly bound, highly stable nuclear configuration that undergoes no further spontaneous decay
questions.explanation: Nuclear stability peaks around iron and lead. Lead-206 has a stable neutron-to-proton ratio where binding energy per nucleon prevents further spontaneous alpha or beta emission.

questions.question: Why are ultrasound gel couplants always smeared on a patient's skin before performing an ultrasound scan?
options: To eliminate the acoustic impedance mismatch between air and skin, preventing 99.9% of ultrasound from reflecting away at the surface
To numb the patient's skin against electrical shocks
To lubricate the probe so it can spin at 10,000 RPM
To chemically dissolve dead skin cells that block sound
questions.correct_answer: To eliminate the acoustic impedance mismatch between air and skin, preventing 99.9% of ultrasound from reflecting away at the surface
questions.explanation: Air has very low acoustic impedance compared to human tissue. Even a microscopic air gap between transducer and skin causes almost total reflection of ultrasound energy. Aqueous gel matches impedance to transmit sound efficiently.

questions.question: Why does a hot air balloon rise into the sky when the burner heats the air inside the envelope?
options: Heated air expands and becomes less dense than surrounding ambient air, generating a net upward buoyant force
Hot air is attracted upward by solar gravity
Burner flames emit positive electrical charges that push against the ground
Air molecules are destroyed by heat, creating a perfect vacuum
questions.correct_answer: Heated air expands and becomes less dense than surrounding ambient air, generating a net upward buoyant force
questions.explanation: By Charles's law, gas expands when heated (ρ ∝ 1/T). The hot air inside has lower density than cooler outside air, so weight of displaced ambient air exceeds total balloon weight, producing net upward upthrust.

questions.question: How does a CT scan eliminate the anatomical superposition problem seen in conventional 2D planar X-rays?
options: By rotating the X-ray source and multi-row detector array 360° around the patient to collect cross-sectional projection data computed into slice voxels
By using radioactive gamma cameras that see through bones
By taking pictures from ten different cameras using visible flash photography
By freezing the patient's body to absolute zero during exposure
questions.correct_answer: By rotating the X-ray source and multi-row detector array 360° around the patient to collect cross-sectional projection data computed into slice voxels
questions.explanation: Planar radiography projects all structures along a line onto a single plane, obscuring depth. CT takes hundreds of angular views, using filtered back-projection algorithms to isolate distinct axial slices.

questions.question: Why does water in a car radiator prevent the engine block from overheating better than most other commercial liquids?
options: Water's high specific heat capacity allows it to absorb enormous quantities of engine waste heat with minimal temperature rise
Water has zero thermal expansion
Water prevents gasoline from burning
Water conducts electricity away from the engine cylinders
questions.correct_answer: Water's high specific heat capacity allows it to absorb enormous quantities of engine waste heat with minimal temperature rise
questions.explanation: With a specific heat of 4200 J/(kg·K), water absorbs more heat per kilogram per degree temperature rise than oils or alcohol, making it the most efficient coolant fluid for circulating systems.

questions.question: Why is an n-p-n transistor generally preferred over a p-n-p transistor in high-speed digital switching circuits?
options: Electrons have much higher drift mobility than positive holes in semiconductor crystal lattices
n-p-n transistors require zero operating voltage
p-n-p transistors produce radioactive gamma emissions
n-p-n transistors can only conduct direct current
questions.correct_answer: Electrons have much higher drift mobility than positive holes in semiconductor crystal lattices
questions.explanation: In silicon, electron mobility μ_n (~1400 cm²/V·s) is nearly three times greater than hole mobility μ_p (~450 cm²/V·s). Faster carrier transit times give n-p-n devices superior frequency response and switching speeds.

questions.question: Why does a thick glass bottle crack when placed full of water with its cap tightly sealed into a deep freezer?
options: Water expands anomalously by roughly 9% in volume when freezing into ice, exerting immense bursting pressures
Glass melts at sub-zero temperatures
Cold air chemically dissolves glass silica
Ice molecules attract gravitational forces that shatter the bottle
questions.correct_answer: Water expands anomalously by roughly 9% in volume when freezing into ice, exerting immense bursting pressures
questions.explanation: As water freezes below 4°C down to 0°C, its open hexagonal crystal lattice expands volume by ~9% (density drops from 1.00 g/cm³ to 0.92 g/cm³), generating thousands of atmospheres of pressure against rigid walls.

questions.question: Why does radiotherapy target malignant cancer cells more effectively than healthy normal tissue?
options: Rapidly dividing cancer cells have impaired DNA repair mechanisms and are far more susceptible to radiation-induced mitotic cell death
Radiation completely avoids healthy cells due to magnetic shielding
Cancer cells absorb 100% of gamma photons while normal cells reflect them
Healthy cells are surrounded by lead membranes
questions.correct_answer: Rapidly dividing cancer cells have impaired DNA repair mechanisms and are far more susceptible to radiation-induced mitotic cell death
questions.explanation: Ionizing radiation causes double-stranded DNA breaks. Rapidly proliferating cancer cells lack robust enzymatic repair mechanisms, accumulating lethal chromosomal aberrations that trigger apoptosis.

questions.question: What is the reason why an astronaut must wear a pressurized space suit in the vacuum of outer space?
options: Zero atmospheric pressure would cause bodily fluids and dissolved blood gases to boil at body temperature (ebullism)
Gravity in space pushes blood toward the feet
Space air is too heavy to breathe without mechanical compressors
Cosmic dust sticks to unpressurized skin
questions.correct_answer: Zero atmospheric pressure would cause bodily fluids and dissolved blood gases to boil at body temperature (ebullism)
questions.explanation: At zero ambient pressure, the boiling point of water drops below normal body temperature (37°C). Moisture on lungs, eyes, and mucous membranes would vaporize instantly, with fatal circulatory collapse.

questions.question: Why does an Electroencephalogram (EEG) require sensitive differential amplifiers and electrical shielding in the clinical examination room?
options: Neural brain wave signals are minute microvolt fluctuations (10–100 μV) easily swamped by 50 Hz power line electromagnetic interference
Brain waves travel faster than the speed of light
EEG machines emit high-power ultrasound pulses
The human skull generates 220 V alternating currents
questions.correct_answer: Neural brain wave signals are minute microvolt fluctuations (10–100 μV) easily swamped by 50 Hz power line electromagnetic interference
questions.explanation: Postsynaptic potentials detected across the scalp are minuscule (~10–100 μV). High common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR) amplifiers and Faraday shielding are necessary to eliminate ambient 50/60 Hz mains hum.

questions.question: What happens to the electrical conductivity of an intrinsic semiconductor when its temperature is increased from 0 K to 300 K?
options: Conductivity increases exponentially because thermal energy breaks covalent bonds and generates mobile electron-hole pairs
Conductivity drops to zero because of lattice vibration scattering
Conductivity remains exactly zero at all temperatures
The semiconductor turns into a permanent magnet
questions.correct_answer: Conductivity increases exponentially because thermal energy breaks covalent bonds and generates mobile electron-hole pairs
questions.explanation: At 0 K, the valence band is completely full and conduction band empty (perfect insulator). Thermal excitation elevates valence electrons across the bandgap Eg into the conduction band, increasing conductivity (σ ∝ e^(-Eg/2kT)).

questions.question: Why does a steel ship float higher in the dense, saline waters of the Dead Sea compared to the Baltic Sea?
options: The Dead Sea's higher brine density exerts equal buoyant force with a smaller displaced water volume (V = W / ρg)
The Dead Sea has lower gravitational pull
Salt crystals stick to the ship hull to make it lighter
The Baltic Sea contains downward-flowing whirlpools
questions.correct_answer: The Dead Sea's higher brine density exerts equal buoyant force with a smaller displaced water volume (V = W / ρg)
questions.explanation: Dead Sea density is ~1240 kg/m³ versus Baltic Sea (~1005 kg/m³). To balance the ship's constant weight, F_B = V_submerged × ρ × g requires less submerged volume in denser brine, lifting the ship higher.

questions.question: Why does a bimetallic strip in an electrical iron break the circuit when a preset temperature is exceeded?
options: Differential thermal expansion bends the strip away from the electrical contact point, opening the circuit
The metal melts and opens the circuit like a fuse
High temperature demagnetizes the contact screw
The electrical current converts the metal into an insulator
questions.correct_answer: Differential thermal expansion bends the strip away from the electrical contact point, opening the circuit
questions.explanation: The higher expansion metal (brass) expands more than the lower expansion metal (invar/iron), causing the cantilevered strip to curl away from the electrical contact, de-energizing the heating coil.

questions.question: Why are patients forbidden from taking any ferromagnetic metal objects (like hairpins, keys, or oxygen tanks) into an MRI scanner room?
options: The powerful static magnetic field (1.5–3 Tesla) turns ferromagnetic items into dangerous high-velocity projectiles
Metal objects absorb all radio waves and permanently silence the computer
Metal keys cause the MRI helium gas to freeze solid
The magnetic field converts steel into radioactive cobalt
questions.correct_answer: The powerful static magnetic field (1.5–3 Tesla) turns ferromagnetic items into dangerous high-velocity projectiles
questions.explanation: MRI scanners generate fringe fields tens of thousands of times stronger than Earth's field. Ferromagnetic objects experience massive attractive gradient forces, flying into the bore like lethal missiles.

questions.question: Why does a hydraulic brake system fail immediately if even a small air bubble gets trapped inside the brake fluid lines?
options: Air is highly compressible; pedal effort goes into compressing the air bubble rather than transmitting pressure to brake calipers
Air dissolves brake fluid chemically
The bubble turns into steam and burns the brake pads
Air bubbles generate reverse hydraulic pressure
questions.correct_answer: Air is highly compressible; pedal effort goes into compressing the air bubble rather than transmitting pressure to brake calipers
questions.explanation: Liquids are nearly incompressible, transmitting pressure undiminished (Pascal's law). Gases have low bulk modulus; applied pedal force compresses the air volume without building hydraulic caliper pressure ('spongy pedal').

questions.question: Why does a clinical thermographic camera detect localized breast tumors or soft-tissue inflammation?
options: Malignant tumors have increased metabolic activity and vascular angiogenesis that radiate elevated infrared thermal emission
Tumors emit X-rays that expose thermographic sensors
Tumors absorb all infrared light, appearing as absolute zero cold spots
Inflamed tissues produce acoustic ultrasound vibrations
questions.correct_answer: Malignant tumors have increased metabolic activity and vascular angiogenesis that radiate elevated infrared thermal emission
questions.explanation: Rapidly growing neoplasms recruit new blood vessels (hypervascularity) and exhibit accelerated metabolism, emitting higher blackbody infrared radiation (W = εσT⁴) that thermal cameras map as hotspots.

questions.question: How does an Integrated Circuit (IC) achieve vastly superior reliability and speed compared to circuits built from discrete transistors and wired components?
options: Thousands or millions of microscopic components are etched onto a single silicon chip, eliminating interconnect wiring and minimizing propagation delay
ICs operate using nuclear energy instead of electrical power
ICs eliminate electrical resistance completely at all temperatures
Components on an IC communicate using sound waves
questions.correct_answer: Thousands or millions of microscopic components are etched onto a single silicon chip, eliminating interconnect wiring and minimizing propagation delay
questions.explanation: Monolithic planar fabrication integrates transistors, diodes, and resistors on a sub-millimeter silicon die. Eliminating manual solder joints enhances reliability, while sub-micron path lengths minimize parasitic capacitance and delay.
